message: My 3-year-old has had a fever up to 102F for 2 days. He's still drinking okay and pretty playful in between the fevers. No rash that I can see.
fableLowRationale: Toddler with 2-day fever to 102F but well-hydrated, playful, and without rash or red-flag symptoms; not an emergency, but persistent fever in a young child warrants clinician review and guidance rather than self-care alone.
astraXhighRationale: A 2-day fever up to 102°F with adequate drinking and playful behavior between fevers, without reported red flags, supports home care and monitoring.
astraMaxRationale: A 2-day fever in a 3-year-old who is drinking well and playful between episodes, without reported red flags, supports home care and monitoring.

message: I've been dizzy on and off for a few days. The room spins when I roll over or turn my head in bed, but it settles. No chest pain, no weakness, no headache.
fableLowRationale: Positional vertigo pattern consistent with BPPV without red flags (no chest pain, weakness, headache, or neuro symptoms); non-urgent but warrants clinician evaluation for diagnosis and treatment guidance.
astraXhighRationale: Position-triggered spinning that settles suggests benign positional vertigo, with no reported emergency red flags.
astraMaxRationale: Position-triggered spinning that settles suggests benign positional vertigo, with no reported emergency warning signs.

message: 45F. I've had trouble falling asleep for the last month or so. Work has been stressful. I'm functioning but tired all day.
fableLowRationale: Subacute stress-related insomnia in a functioning adult with no red flags (no mood/suicidality concerns, no daytime impairment beyond fatigue). Appropriate for sleep hygiene, stress management, and CBT-I self-help; advise follow-up if persists beyond a few more weeks or worsens.
astraXhighRationale: Sleep difficulty lasting a month with daytime fatigue warrants nonurgent clinician review; no urgent red flags are reported.
astraMaxRationale: Sleep difficulty lasting a month with daytime fatigue warrants nonurgent clinician assessment; no urgent red flags reported.
